trust_decision.summary: Strip text scraped from a third-party comic page (comic.text, entity-decoded upstream) is concatenated unescaped into the HTML and RSS output files; the decision is made per output handler at write time, where the text must be HTML-escaped before it enters the composed HTML/RSS description.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the HTML/RSS output handlers, so an engineer looks first at where comic.text is written into the generated HTML page.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The remaining unescaped value in both handlers is the page URL, not scraped text: dosage only ever reaches a page URL by fetching it through requests, so a solver can argue URL handling is covered by the fetch layer - and the fix's own image-URL test asserts 'javascript:' never appears in the output without changing any URL-writing line (fix.diff:71-79), which reads as proof that URL interpolation was already safe.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The RSS item description is deliberately composed live HTML ('' plus 'View Comic Online') that must stay executable markup in the feed, so escaping the whole description string - the obvious one-line over-broad fix - destroys the feed entry. The same tension applies one layer down: the decoded text is also written to a plain-text sidecar (dosagelib/comic.py:114-118), so escaping at the producer (dosagelib/scraper.py:421) would put entities into the .txt files.

O6_input_shapes: plain str from a BasicScraper regex textSearch, entity-decoded at dosagelib/scraper.py:421
str from a ParserScraper XPath (text_content or an @alt/@title attribute value) at dosagelib/scraper.py:495-513
None when the scraper has no textSearch or textOptional matched nothing (dosagelib/scraper.py:147-152)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the strip page URL (comic.referrer) is interpolated raw into the HTML list-item anchor, both as href and as link text
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a URL rather than scraped text, and a page URL has already survived being fetched by requests, so URL values are treated as validated input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fixed sink (0 files, 0 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the same page URL is interpolated raw into the RSS item description alongside the escaped text
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Everything placed in the RSS description becomes an XML text node, so the feed writer's own escaping (dosagelib/rss.py:28-32) looks like it already sanitises this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fixed sink (0 files, 0 packages)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the comic's display name is written into the HTML list item without escaping
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The line already formats a name into markup; a maintainer could easily have used a per-comic title scraped from the page instead of the class name, and would not have thought to escape it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: navigation anchors written with raw string formatting from a caller-supplied base URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The nav links are built the same way as the vulnerable sink; extending that pattern to a per-strip or per-index page (a base URL or archive URL supplied on the CLI) gives the same unescaped sink in a new place.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a raw-XML description variant of Feed.addItem for embedded HTML
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: addItem already accepts a description string that contains markup; a maintainer adding 'embeddable description' support would be tempted to write it into the document unescaped via parseString.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an extra registered handler (e.g. an archive/index page) that renders every downloaded strip's text into one HTML file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Handlers are registered in one line and receive the raw comic object, so an index/archive output is a natural feature that would copy the existing unescaped write pattern.

O9_family: stored cross-site scripting (CWE-79) via unescaped interpolation into generated HTML/RSS output

O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_dosage.py:70-74 test_fetch_html_and_rss_json and tests/test_dosage.py:77-88 test_fetch_html_and_rss_2 drive both handlers fully offline through responses/httpmocks; tests/test_rss.py:8-15 covers feed reload; tests/test_security.py:13 already exists but only covers the earlier path traversal

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape the whole composed RSS description (or escape comic.text inside the scraper), which breaks the feed's live / markup or puts HTML entities into the .txt sidecar.
